When should agents talk? A selective-exposure, evidence-composition account of staged retrieval-mediated Q/A under matched compute

1. The puzzle and the thesis

Three recent empirical results look mutually incompatible. Du et al. report multi-agent debate beating majority voting by ~13 points on arithmetic (81.8±2.3 vs 69.0±4.6) and ~21 pawn-score points on chess, with 3 agents and 2 rounds (papers/text/du-et-al-2023-multiagent-debate.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 6 =====). Smit et al. find that debate protocols, including Du's own Society of Minds, "do not reliably outperform" self-consistency and ensembling (papers/text/smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 1 =====). Zhang et al., the only study that explicitly aligns LLM-call budgets, find no debate method wins more than 20% of 36 model×benchmark scenarios against chain-of-thought, and that the deficit "becomes even more pronounced when compared to SC, especially when using a comparable number of LLM calls or tokens" (papers/text/zhang-et-al-2025-mad-question.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 3 =====). Yet Zhang also find that mixing models inside debate (Heter-MAD) improves every framework tested, by +6.4% to +8.2% over single-model averages (===== PDF PAGE 11 =====), while conceding that current benchmarks "require only a single knowledge point" and that tasks needing distributed knowledge may suit debate (===== PDF PAGE 14-15 =====).

This note defends one mechanistic thesis. Under matched total inference compute, staged retrieval-mediated Q/A outperforms both independent sampling with final aggregation and an open shared transcript if and only if three conditions hold jointly: (i) the task is compositional — reaching the answer requires combining k>1 complementary evidence units that are initially distributed across agents; (ii) agents' errors are sufficiently decorrelated that the population collectively holds the units even though no individual or majority does; and (iii) exposure to peers is gated — agents retrieve question-relevant peer content rather than reading a full transcript — so that diversity is preserved long enough to be composed, and retrieval supplies external evidence that pure answer-adjudication cannot. The mechanism is evidence routing under an exposure budget, not deliberation. Independent sampling has zero conformity cost but a composition ceiling (voting cannot assemble parts nobody holds wholly); an open transcript has no ceiling but pays a conformity tax that collapses the diversity it needs. Staged retrieval-mediated Q/A is the only condition that buys composition without paying the full tax. This is a hypothesis, not an established result; the corpus constrains but does not test it.

2. Reconciling the corpus

Reported findings first. Du's debate gains are real but confounded: the paper concedes debate is "more costly, requiring multiple model instances and rounds" (papers/text/du-et-al-2023-multiagent-debate.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 2 =====), and at 3 agents/2 rounds debate consumes ~9 generations versus ~3 for majority voting — roughly 3x compute (my inference from the procedure, ===== PDF PAGE 4 =====; the paper never quantifies cost). Its weakest headline gap, GSM8K (85.0 vs 81.0, overlapping error bars, ===== PDF PAGE 6 =====), is exactly the kind that vanishes under compute matching. Du also reports the adverse signature: debate converges to answers that are "not necessarily correct," with agents confidently affirming wrong consensuses (===== PDF PAGE 10 =====), and reflection baselines sometimes hurt (MMLU 57.7 vs 63.9 single-agent, ===== PDF PAGE 7 =====). Smit et al. add that debate's benefit is hyperparameter- and dataset-contingent: a K-fold selection flips the winner between medical and non-medical groups (papers/text/smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 5 =====); Multi-Persona's forced-disagreeing devil agent reduces accuracy below its own first answer (===== PDF PAGE 6 =====); and prompting "agreement intensity" helps on MedQA/PubMedQA but hurts on counter-intuitive CIAR — a sign flip in how conformity affects accuracy (===== PDF PAGE 6 =====). Zhang et al. then show the reconciliation's spine: debate beats direct single-agent prompting in 34 of 45 GPT-4o-mini conditions, "which perfectly aligns with previous findings" (papers/text/zhang-et-al-2025-mad-question.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 8 =====), but the original positive papers never compared against CoT, and at matched budgets SC dominates. Scaling agents 3→9 or rounds 2→4 mostly stagnates or declines (===== PDF PAGE 9 =====), and aggressive protocols correct many errors while flipping many correct answers — a correction/instability trade-off (===== PDF PAGE 9 =====).

The conflict dissolves under two moderators: baseline strength/compute matching, and task topology. All three papers are consistent with: communication beats the weakest baseline, matches or loses to decorrelated sampling at matched compute on single-knowledge tasks, and has a contingency that prior work attributes vaguely to "hyperparameters."

Two social-influence papers supply the conformity pathway. Lorenz et al. show in humans that bare numerical feedback — no persuasion, leaders, or conformity premium — "strongly reduces the group's diversity without significantly reducing its collective errors," while boosting confidence (papers/text/lorenz-et-al-2011-social-influence.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 3 =====, ===== PDF PAGE 5 =====). Choi et al. show LLM conformity is real but capability-dominated: majority size has a moderate effect (eta_p2≈0.068) while model capability has a large one (eta_p2≈0.167), and one strong agent beats two weak ones (papers/text/choi-et-al-2025-conformity.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 6-7 =====). Critically, Choi's topics lack ground truth and every condition exposes agents to full arguments, so it measures rationale-accompanied persuasion, not error change.

Two formal papers constrain the synthesis stage. Dung's argumentation semantics guarantee that conflicting answers can be adjudicated only relationally: under symmetric mutual attack there are two preferred extensions and an empty grounded one — "a skeptical reasoner will not include anything" — and the framework deliberately excludes evidential weight or attack strength, which Dung leaves to future work (papers/text/dung-1995-argumentation.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 7 =====, ===== PDF PAGE 9 =====, ===== PDF PAGE 31 =====). Shapiro et al. show merge rules are truth-neutral in the same way: add-wins, remove-wins, or reset-to-bottom all satisfy strong convergence, and "any of them may be reasonable for some application" (papers/text/shapiro-et-al-2011-crdts.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 8 =====); the CRDT convergence theorems require commutative, idempotent merge operators (===== PDF PAGE 5-6 =====), which stochastic LLM synthesis plausibly violates. Agreement, convergence, and merge success are therefore structural properties, never evidence of truth.

3. Causal model

Variables: rho_e, initial error correlation across agents; D, effective diversity of evidence units in the population; S, social-influence pressure (exposure volume × rationale richness × capability asymmetry); R, retrieval selectivity (precision/recall of staged fetch against the needed units); C, synthesis competence; T, task topology indexed by k, the number of complementary units required.

Pathways. T gates everything: at k=1 a single correct sample suffices, so sampling plus vote is near-optimal and communication spend is waste — this is Zhang's null. Given k>1, low rho_e and high D mean the units exist but scattered; composition value rises. Communication condition then sets S: an open transcript maximizes exposure, triggering the Lorenz collapse of D without error reduction, amplified toward high-capability agents per Choi — which corrects errors when the strong agent is right and amplifies them when wrong. Staged retrieval-mediated Q/A keeps S low (agents see only fetched, question-relevant content) while R moves the needed units to the synthesizer. R also does the job Dung proves adjudication cannot: breaking symmetric answer-ties with external evidence. C, bounded by Dung (needs weights it cannot derive) and Shapiro (non-commutative synthesis adds order-variance), converts assembled units into a final answer. Net: accuracy gain from communication ≈ composition value (rising in k, D, R) − conformity cost (rising in S) − synthesis variance (falling in C). Sampling sets the first term to ~0 and the second to 0; transcript maximizes the second; staged Q/A is engineered to maximize the first while suppressing the second.

4. Discriminating predictions

P1 (topology interaction). The staged-Q/A minus matched-compute-SC accuracy gap is ≤0 on k=1 strata and >0 on k≥2 strata, monotone in k. Compute-only predicts no condition beats SC anywhere; diversity-only predicts pool heterogeneity matters but not k; deliberation-only predicts benefits wherever disagreement exists, regardless of k.

P2 (exposure vs rationale). Holding retrieved evidence fixed, exposing agents to peers' bare answers increases answer-shift toward the majority and inflates confidence without improving accuracy on hard items (the Lorenz signature), whereas adding rationales increases shift further — per Choi — with accuracy rising only when the rationale source is correct. Deliberation-only predicts rationale exposure should improve accuracy on average; diversity-only predicts no exposure effect at all.

P3 (heterogeneity control). Against a heterogeneous-SC control (each sample from a distinct model, majority vote, no communication — the control Zhang omitted), staged Q/A wins only on high-k strata, and the margin grows with measured retrieval recall. If heterogeneous SC matches staged Q/A everywhere at matched budget, the thesis collapses into diversity-only.

P4 (retrieval as tie-breaker). On items where the population splits into two symmetric, mutually contradicting camps (a Dung diamond), staged Q/A with evidence retrieval resolves the tie above chance; removing retrieval while holding agents, rounds, and compute fixed collapses the advantage to ~0, because grounded adjudication is empty. Deliberation-only predicts debate without retrieval resolves such ties too.

P5 (synthesis variance). Permuting the order of agent contributions changes the output of an LLM synthesizer measurably, while vote/union aggregators are invariant (Shapiro diagnostic); final-answer variance under permutation predicts the staged condition's error tail, so deterministic aggregation should dominate stochastic synthesis at equal budget unless C is demonstrably high.

5. What the existing evidence cannot identify

No corpus study jointly manipulates communication structure, task topology, and compute with verifiable ground truth. Du never runs a compute-matched comparison, uses ~100-item evaluations, and scores biographies with chatGPT itself, risking circularity (papers/text/du-et-al-2023-multiagent-debate.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 13 =====). Smit frames trade-offs in cost, not matched compute, relies on a nondeterministic public API, and never tests agreement-tuned gains at equal API calls (papers/text/smit-et-al-2023-going-mad.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 9 =====). Zhang counts ANOVA p>0.05 as a tie with only three repetitions, inflating tie rates under low power, and omits the heterogeneous-SC control that would separate decorrelation from deliberation (papers/text/zhang-et-al-2025-mad-question.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 3 =====, ===== PDF PAGE 11 =====). Lorenz is human evidence with no rationales and no compute notion, its aggregated-vs-full ordering confounded by biased arithmetic-mean feedback, and its moderation analyses sit in an SI outside the corpus (papers/text/lorenz-et-al-2011-social-influence.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 3 =====, ===== PDF PAGE 5 =====). Choi measures persuasion on ground-truth-free topics, operationalizes "intelligence" as parameter size confounded with provider, and offers no bare-answer condition (papers/text/choi-et-al-2025-conformity.txt, ===== PDF PAGE 4-5 =====). Dung and Shapiro are formal, not empirical; mapping answers to arguments and merges to CRDTs is this note's operationalization. Consequently, four things remain unidentified: whether LLM conformity requires rationales or mere answer exposure (the Lorenz–Choi fork); whether heterogeneity gains exceed decorrelated sampling (Zhang's missing control); whether the SC dominance reverses on genuinely compositional tasks (Zhang's untested conjecture); and whether capability-driven conformity on verifiable tasks is error-correcting or error-amplifying.

6. A preregisterable experiment

Units and strata. Item = one question with a verified gold answer; cluster = one agent group. Three task strata by verified compositionality k: k=1 (single-fact/single-chain items, e.g., MMLU/GSM8K-style); k=2–3 and k≥4 constructed compositional QA in which the required evidence units are partitioned so that no agent's context contains all units — validated by ablation (a single agent given the full partition solves ≥85%; given any proper subset, ≤40%). k verified per item before randomization.

Conditions and compute matching. Factorial: 3 communication conditions × 2 pools. Conditions: (A) staged retrieval-mediated Q/A — agents answer independently, post structured queries, fetch top-m peer content via a fixed retriever, then a synthesizer answers; (B) independent sampling + majority vote (SC); (C) open shared transcript with rounds. Pools: homogeneous (one model) and heterogeneous (two capability-matched models, assignment randomized). Total inference budget B (generated + processed tokens, audited per item) equalized across conditions; B set at two levels (6 and 12 calls-equivalent) to check budget robustness.

Randomization. Stratified block randomization of items to conditions within (stratum × difficulty quartile), each item run under all conditions with distinct seeds (crossover) plus between-item replicates; agent-to-model assignment, speaking order, and retrieval tie-breaks randomized; decoding parameters fixed.

Intervention fidelity. Log per agent: number of peer answers and rationales seen (exposure), retrieval precision/recall against the gold partition, pre/post answer-shifts toward the majority (conformity), and order/duplication permutation tests on the synthesizer (Shapiro diagnostic). Fidelity thresholds preregistered: retrieval recall ≥0.70; exposure in C ≥3× A.

Estimands and outcomes. Primary: item-level accuracy difference A−B within k≥2 strata at matched B (intention-to-treat over assigned conditions). Key secondary: the (A−B)×k interaction; A−C (conformity-tax estimate); heterogeneity×communication interaction (the Zhang-missing control); diversity retained (effective unique answers post-exposure); confidence–accuracy calibration; synthesis order-variance.

Power inputs. Binary outcome, baseline accuracy ~0.60 (Zhang's Table 3 range), smallest effect of interest 0.06 (below Heter-MAD's +6.4–8.2%). For the primary contrast at alpha=0.05 two-sided, 80% power: ~1,050 items per arm without clustering; the crossover design and mixed model reduce this; plan 1,200 items per cell in k≥2 strata, 600 in k=1 (powered for the interaction, not only main effects). ICC from item clustering assumed ≤0.05; design effect reported.

Exclusions, multiplicity, stopping. Preregistered exclusions, applied blind to condition: API/parse failures, items failing partition validation, groups violating exposure floors. One primary confirmatory contrast; Holm correction within the secondary family; no other inferential claims. Futility: if at 50% data the 95% CI for the primary contrast lies entirely below +0.02, stop for futility. Fidelity failure (recall <0.70) triggers redesign, not inference. Analysis: logistic mixed model, accuracy ~ condition×stratum×pool + (1|item) + (1|group), with preregistered decision rules mapping outcomes to mechanisms — diversity-only if heterogeneous SC ≈ A everywhere; deliberation-only if A wins uniformly in k; compute-only if nothing beats B anywhere; the present thesis only if the k-interaction, retrieval-necessity, and exposure-gating patterns jointly obtain.

7. Conclusion, open questions, and the falsifier

Strongest warranted conclusion: on current evidence, debate-style communication at matched compute does not beat decorrelated sampling on the single-knowledge tasks that dominate benchmarks, and open-transcript exposure carries a demonstrated diversity-collapse risk with no accuracy compensation. The only defensible niche for staged retrieval-mediated Q/A is compositional tasks with distributed evidence and decorrelated errors, where gated exposure preserves the diversity that transcripts destroy and retrieval supplies the external weight that answer-adjudication provably lacks. Material open questions: the exposure-vs-rationale fork, the missing heterogeneous-SC control, the untested topology reversal, the direction of capability-driven conformity on verifiable tasks, and the order-stability of LLM synthesis. The single observation most likely to falsify the thesis: heterogeneous self-consistency matching staged retrieval-mediated Q/A at matched compute on high-k compositional strata — if decorrelated samples alone capture everything the population knows, communication adds nothing, and the mechanism is dead.

answer:work:001-inv-du-debate.summary: Du et al. 2023 (arXiv:2305.14325v1, 'Preprint. Under review', PDF p1) propose that multiple instances of the same LLM independently answer a query, then iteratively update their answers after seeing other agents' concatenated responses (short/long consensus prompts, Fig 3, PDF p4), converging to a shared final answer. TASKS (six, all gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, zero-shot; eval details PDF p13): reasoning — (1) Arithmetic (six random integers 0–30 in a+b*c+d-e*f; 100 tasks, PDF pp5,13), (2) GSM8K (100 problems, PDF pp5,13), (3) Chess Move Prediction (best 15th move after 14 PGN moves; Stockfish pawn score depth 20; 300 games, PDF pp5,13); factuality — (4) Biographies (new benchmark, 524 computer scientists, bullet facts vs Wikipedia ground truth scored by chatGPT yes/no/uncertain, PDF pp6,13), (5) MMLU (100 questions, PDF pp7,13), (6) Chess Move Validity (BIG-Bench chess-state tracking, PDF p7). BASELINES (PDF p5): Single Agent; Single Agent + Reflection; Multi-Agent (Majority) — majority vote over multiple agents' independent generations; debate uses identical starting prompt/model; majority baseline omitted for factuality tasks because responses aren't comparable (PDF p7). MAIN RESULTS (3 agents, 2 rounds, Table 1 PDF p6): Arithmetic 81.8±2.3 debate vs 69.0±4.6 majority, 67.0±4.7 single, 72.1±4.5 reflection; GSM8K 85.0±3.5 vs 81.0±3.9 majority, 77.0±4.2 single (reflection 75.0 hurts); Chess ΔPS 122.9±7.6 vs 102.2±6.2 majority, 91.4±10.6 single. So debate beats majority voting by ~13 points on arithmetic and ~21 pawn-score points on chess, but only ~4 points (within overlapping error bars) on GSM8K. FACTUALITY (Table 2 PDF p7): Biographies 73.8 vs 66.0 single; MMLU 71.1 vs 63.9; Chess Validity 45.2 vs 29.3; reflection underperforms single agent on MMLU (57.7). SCALING: headline config is 3 agents/2 rounds 'due to computational expense', but accuracy rises with agents (1→5, with summarization for 5+) and rounds (1→4) (Fig 10, PDF pp5,8); longer/stubborner prompts slow convergence but improve final accuracy (Fig 12, PDF p8); summarizing other agents' responses improves over concatenation (Fig 13, PDF p8); personas raise MMLU 71.1→74.2 (PDF p8); ChatGPT+Bard debate on 20 GSM8K problems: Bard 11, ChatGPT 14, debate 17 (PDF pp8-9). CONSENSUS: convergence to a single answer is not guaranteed in theory but observed empirically; agents are 'relatively agreeable', attributed to instruction tuning/RLHF (PDF p4); uncertain facts produce divergent initial answers that debate collapses to one 'more accurate, but not necessarily always factually correct' answer (Fig 9, PDF p8); confidently-held facts resist persuasion, so 'ease of persuasion' is proposed as a confidence probe (PDF p7); short prompts yield faster consensus (Fig 14, PDF p13); debate can flip all-initially-wrong populations to correct (PDF pp2,6). FAILURE MODES: debate sometimes converges to a wrong value that agents confidently affirm (PDF p10 limitations; incorrect-debate examples Figs 21-23, PDF p13); long debates cause models to attend only to recent generations (PDF p10). COMPUTE: the paper concedes debate is 'more costly, requiring multiple model instances and rounds' (PDF p2) and 'more computationally expensive' than other prompting techniques (PDF p10); it reports NO compute-matched comparison — majority voting at 3 agents costs ~3 generations vs debate's ~9 (3 initial + 6 updates), so the debate-vs-majority gap is confounded by roughly 3x inference compute (my inference from the procedure, PDF p4; the paper never quantifies tokens).

answer:work:001-inv-lorenz-influence.summary: Lorenz, Rauhut, Schweitzer & Helbing (PNAS 2011, N=144) ran a lab experiment isolating how minimal social influence degrades collective estimation. DESIGN (PDF PAGE 2, 5, 6): 12 sessions of 12 ETH Zurich students each answered six factual estimation questions (Swiss population density, Swiss-Italian border length, Zurich immigration 2006, murders/rapes/assaults registered in Switzerland 2006), chosen to be moderately difficult (only 1.5% of runs always in the top reward band). Each question was answered in five consecutive private rounds from isolated cubicles; confidence (6-point Likert) was elicited after rounds 1 and 5 and never shared. Monetary rewards (4/2/1 points = 1.40/0.70/0.35 CHF for estimates within 10/20/40% of truth, all rounds paid) were deliberately non-competitive so others' estimates could only be used to approach truth, not to conform for gain. Three within-session information conditions, order randomized: (i) NO INFORMATION control — re-answer five times, reminded only of own last estimate; (ii) AGGREGATED INFORMATION — see the arithmetic mean of all 12 estimates from the previous round; (iii) FULL INFORMATION — see a figure of all 12 individual estimate trajectories over all previous rounds plus last-round numerical values. Per treatment: 24 groups (4 per question). THREE SIGNATURE EFFECTS: (1) Social influence effect — estimates converge and group diversity is strongly, significantly reduced (KS and F tests) WITHOUT significant reduction of collective error; effects 'almost null' in control (PDF PAGE 3, Fig 1D/E). (2) Range reduction effect — a wisdom-of-crowd indicator (centrality of the truth among sorted estimates; max 6 for n=12) declines over rounds with information exchange; regression over all questions: ~1 unit lower than control, and the decline is STRONGER under aggregated than full information, which authors link to gossip-from-fewer-sources findings (PDF PAGE 4-5). (3) Confidence effect — confidence is significantly boosted in both information conditions vs control, despite no accuracy gains: 'subjective' reliability rises as 'objective' reliability falls, a psychological trap (PDF PAGE 4 caption, PAGE 5). WHEN INFLUENCE HELPED VS UNDERMINED: it undermined in all three ways whenever questions were hard/uncertain, but there was a slight collective-error decline, especially in the aggregated condition, which the authors attribute to an artifact: right-skewed estimates make the arithmetic mean feedback higher than most estimates and above the truth, while the geometric mean of first estimates sits slightly below the truth, so mean feedback induces an upward drift toward truth — 'this effect may be different for different sets of questions' (PDF PAGE 3 footnote). Undermining was 'less severe for easier questions and if individuals are more confident' (SI Appendix, cited PDF PAGE 5). Aggregation note: arithmetic mean beat individual first estimates in only 21.3% of cases; geometric mean in 77.1% (log-transform justified by right-skew); Table 1 gives per-question aggregates (PDF PAGE 3). AUTHORS' INTERPRETATION: even bare numerical feedback — no persuasion, leaders, or strategic incentives — triggers herding; diversity loss 'appears to be a necessary byproduct of transparent decision-making processes'; convergence breeds collective overconfidence (PDF PAGE 5). CAVEATS: initial diversity was higher in control (possible anticipatory conservatism, mainly crime questions); 10 of 864x5 values removed (outliers, 'fun moves'); human students, six right-skewed estimation tasks only (PDF PAGE 3, 5-6).

answer:work:002-inv-choi-r2.summary: Choi et al. 2025 (ACL Findings) ran >2,500 structured LLM debates on five ground-truth-free social topics with proponent, opponent, and neutral (always GPT-4o) agents, manipulating group size (1:2, 2:1, up to 1:8) and 'intelligence' (parameter size, large vs small models from GPT/Claude/Qwen). Neutral agents conform significantly to numerical majorities (chi2=164.839, p<0.001; CR 63.5-72.1% at 2:1 vs 39.4-42.2% at 1:2) and to higher-intelligence sides (chi2=142.285, p<0.001; CR 74.3% when the proponent is the large model vs 39.8% when it is small). Critically, intelligence dominates numbers: one large-model agent against two small-model agents still wins 66.3% of turns, while two small agents against one large win only 42.2%; effect size for intelligence (eta_p2~0.167, large) dwarfs majority size (~0.068, moderate), and more capable evaluators (GPT-4o-mini vs GPT-3.5-turbo) are less swayed by headcount as ratios scale to 1:8. Authors conclude argument quality outweighs quantity. However, every condition exposes the neutral to full 256-token persuasive arguments across 3 turns; there is no bare-answer condition, so the paper cannot discriminate answer-only exposure from rationale-mediated influence (rq1 remains open; Choi only bounds it from the rationale side). Conformity here is evaluator persuasion on opinion topics, not accuracy change on verifiable tasks.

answer:work:002-inv-dung-r2.summary: Dung 1995 supplies exactly the formal vocabulary for the 'synthesis competence' node: an argumentation framework AF = (AR, attacks) treats answers as abstract atoms linked by a binary attack relation, with no internal structure, weight, or truth value. Admissibility (a conflict-free set that defends every member against all attackers) is the core rationality constraint; on top of it Dung defines a lattice of semantics with different guarantees: preferred extensions (maximal admissible sets; always at least one exists, but symmetric conflicts like the Nixon diamond yield several, so credulous justification is non-unique), stable extensions (conflict-free sets attacking every outside argument; strictly stronger than preferred and may fail to exist at all), and the grounded extension (least fixed point of the characteristic function F_AF(S) = {A | A acceptable wrt S}; always unique, but can be empty — the skeptical adjudicator may justifiably endorse nothing when two agent answers attack each other symmetrically). Complete extensions bridge the two: every preferred extension is complete, and the grounded extension is the least complete one. The key coincidence result for adjudication design: well-founded frameworks (no infinite attack chains) have exactly one extension that is simultaneously grounded, preferred, and stable — the formal condition under which conflict adjudication is unambiguous. Equally important for the note: the framework deliberately does NOT model evidential weight, attack strength, truth, or probabilistic confidence — Dung himself lists differentiating attack strength as necessary future work. Consequence for the research problem: Dung-style adjudication can tell a synthesizer which set of conflicting agent answers is defensible, but it cannot break symmetric ties (two mutually attacking answers produce two preferred extensions and an empty grounded one); whatever breaks the tie — retrieval of external evidence, in our mechanism — is precisely what the formalism lacks and what retrieval-mediated Q/A supplies. The wave-1 combined Dung+Shapiro packet failed with zero evidence (blocked, 'Exceeded maximum output retries'), so this packet is the sole source for the Dung half.

answer:work:002-inv-shapiro-r2.summary: Shapiro et al. 2011 formalize exactly the merge/aggregation stage of any multi-agent pipeline: how concurrent contributions combine without central coordination. Core machinery: (1) A Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT) is a replicated data type whose design satisfies sufficient conditions for Strong Eventual Consistency (SEC); SEC = eventual consistency (eventual delivery, convergence, termination) plus Strong Convergence — correct replicas that have delivered the same updates have equivalent state immediately, with no consensus, no roll-back, and no waiting for quiescence (Defs. 2–3, page 4). (2) Two sufficient conditions: state-based CvRDT — payload forms a join semilattice, merge computes the least upper bound (commutative, idempotent, associative), and state is monotonically non-decreasing; Theorem 1 gives SEC assuming eventual delivery and termination (pages 4–5). Op-based CmRDT — updates split into a side-effect-free prepare step at the source and an effect-update delivered downstream; if all concurrent updates commute and delivery is reliable and causally ordered, Theorem 2 gives SEC (pages 5–6). (3) The two styles are mutually emulatable (Theorems 3–4, pages 7–8), so 'merge states' vs 'merge operations' is an implementation choice, not a difference in guarantee. (4) Scope and limits: SEC solves the CAP dilemma by staying available and partition-tolerant without consensus, tolerating n−1 crashes (page 6); but eventual delivery alone is insufficient (no-op merge counterexample, page 4), and SEC is incomparable with sequential consistency — the converged state need not correspond to any sequential execution (page 8). Crucially for the research note, the guarantees are truth-neutral: correctness is defined relative to a chosen concurrent specification, not relative to fact. Add-wins, remove-wins, highest-IP-wins, or reset-to-⊥ all satisfy strong convergence ('any of them may be reasonable for some application', page 8); LWW imposes a total order 'at the cost of losing concurrent updates' (page 13). Cross-paper inference for the note (not Shapiro's claim): both independent-sampling-plus-aggregation and staged Q/A must pick a merge rule for agent contributions, and CRDT theory shows that rule choice determines which contributions survive aggregation while saying nothing about whether the merged content is true — formally grounding the dossier constraint that agreement or merge success is not evidence of correctness. A further diagnostic for the note: LLM free-text synthesis is generally neither commutative nor idempotent, so it fails the CRDT sufficient conditions and inherits no convergence guarantee at all.
unresolved: Whether any aggregation operator actually used in multi-agent LLM systems (majority vote, evidence-union, LLM free-text synthesis) satisfies commutativity/idempotence/monotonicity; LLM synthesis plausibly violates all three, meaning staged Q/A and independent+aggregation pipelines may have no convergence guarantee of the CRDT kind — a diagnostic the research note should exploit but this extraction cannot settle.
The paper gives no guidance on merging weighted, probabilistic, or natural-language content; adapting semilattice machinery to confidence-bearing claims is open.

answer:work:002-inv-smit-mad-r2.summary: Smit et al. 2023 (ICML 2024, arXiv:2311.17371v3) benchmark three MAD protocols — Society of Mind (Du et al. 2023), Multi-Persona (Liang et al. 2023, angel/devil/judge), ChatEval's three modes (Chan et al. 2023) — against non-debate multi-call strategies (Self-Consistency, Ensemble Refinement, Medprompt without its kNN component) and Single Agent, crossed with five agent-level prompts, on seven multiple-choice datasets (MedQA 1273, PubMedQA 500, MMLU-clinical 123, CosmosQA 500, CIAR 50, GPQA 448, Chess-short 1000), primarily GPT-3.5-turbo with GPT-4/Mixtral-8x7B checks on MedQA. Cost is USD per question and average API calls per question (plus time and prompt length in appendices). Headline: with original implementations MAD does not reliably beat Self-Consistency or Medprompt (Medprompt best overall: MedQA 0.65, PubMedQA 0.77; Single Agent best on GPQA 0.33; no protocol dominates all datasets), and MAD uses more API calls/tokens/cost. A K-fold analysis (pick hyperparameters best on two held-out same-category datasets) flips the winner between medical and non-medical groups, showing optimal settings are dataset-specific and no protocol is assured to beat single-agent on new data. Debate-vs-first-answer gains are protocol-dependent: SoM gains substantially, ChatEval modestly, Multi-Persona loses accuracy because the devil agent disagrees even with correct first answers. The paper's own mechanism claim: prompting 'agreement intensity' modulates first-round agreement and accuracy, with dataset-dependent sign — high agreement helps MedQA/PubMedQA, disagreement helps counter-intuitive CIAR; tuning yields ~15% for Multi-Persona and ~5% for SoM on a 376-question USMLE subset, and 90%-agreement Multi-Persona sets a claimed GPT-3 state-of-the-art on full MedQA. Hyperparameters transfer GPT-3.5→GPT-4 but not to Mixtral-8x7B. Stated limitations: API nondeterminism/model updates; cost-limited scale.
unresolved: The optimal hyperparameter configuration per dataset (which K-fold selected) is in Appendix A.2/Table 3 but was not exhaustively transcribed; only representative rows were read.
Whether the agreement-modulation gain survives a strictly compute-matched comparison against self-consistency at equal API calls is not tested in the paper.

answer:work:002-inv-zhang-when-r2.summary: Zhang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2502.08788v3; position paper subtitled 'Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate—We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity') is the corpus's decisive matched-compute reappraisal. DESIGN: 5 MAD frameworks (SoM=Du et al. 2023, Multi-Persona, Exchange-of-Thoughts, ChatEval, AgentVerse) x 9 benchmarks (general knowledge: MMLU, MMLU-Pro, CommonsenseQA, ARC-Challenge, AGIEval; math: GSM8K, MATH; programming: HumanEval, MBPP) x 4 models (GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-haiku, Llama3.1-8b, Llama3.1-70b), vs SA/CoT/SC baselines, debate rounds adjusted so every MAD method uses ~6 LLM calls; 3 repetitions with std (===== PDF PAGE 1, 6, 7 =====). HEADLINE: no MAD method exceeds a 20% win rate vs CoT across 36 scenarios; SoM/EoT/ChatEval/AgentVerse win ~15%, MP 0%; worse on programming, relatively better on math; the gap widens vs self-consistency at comparable LLM-call or token budgets (===== PDF PAGE 3, 7-8 =====). RECONCILIATION: MAD beats direct single-agent prompting in 34/45 GPT-4o-mini conditions—'perfectly aligns with previous findings'—but SoM and ChatEval were never compared to CoT in their original papers, so Du-style positives hold only against the weakest baseline (===== PDF PAGE 8 =====). HYPERPARAMETERS: agents 3->9, rounds 2->4 yield mostly stagnation or decline (sole exception EoT on GSM8K), ruling out misconfiguration as a universal explanation (===== PDF PAGE 8-9 =====). EFFICIENCY: SC converts extra tokens into accuracy; MAD is flat (SoM on MMLU) or trails SC at comparable tokens (EoT); per-question analysis shows aggressive methods (MP/ChatEval/AgentVerse) correct many errors but flip many correct answers, while conservative ones (SoM/EoT) avoid new errors but correct few—a correction/instability trade-off (===== PDF PAGE 9, 25 =====). HETEROGENEITY: Heter-MAD (each generation queries a random model from {GPT-4o-mini, Llama3.1-70b}, p=0.5) improves every tested framework (+6.4% SoM, +8.2% EoT vs single-model averages; up to +5.8% vs CoT-Average), with gains concentrated where models have complementary solvability and in simpler frameworks—'a universal antidote' (===== PDF PAGE 1, 4, 10-13 =====). POSITIONING: credits Du et al. 2023 as foundational but attributes MAD's overvaluation to fragmented, selective evaluation (Table 5 shows minimal benchmark overlap across prior MAD papers); aligns with Smit et al. 2024's null while dismissing its medical-only scope; flags that agents debate whole responses yet rebut final-answer differences rather than reasoning, and that current benchmarks need only single knowledge points (===== PDF PAGE 2, 5, 13, 14, 15 =====). Key identification gap for the root note: no heterogeneous self-consistency control, so the debate-specific value of heterogeneity over plain decorrelated sampling is not identified.
unresolved: Whether heterogeneous self-consistency (mixed-model sampling + majority vote, no communication) matches Heter-MAD at matched calls/tokens — the control needed to attribute heterogeneity gains to debate rather than to error decorrelation alone.

Why aggressive MAD variants flip initially correct answers: Zhang's corrected/erred analysis is behavioral and cannot distinguish social-influence conformity (Lorenz/Choi-style) from noise amplification or judge/aggregation failures.
Whether task topology (benchmarks requiring multiple, complementary knowledge points) reverses the MAD vs SC ordering — Zhang conjectures yes ('===== PDF PAGE 14 =====') but tests nothing.

root_packet.account: Zhang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2502.08788v3; position paper subtitled 'Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate—We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity') is the corpus's decisive matched-compute reappraisal. DESIGN: 5 MAD frameworks (SoM=Du et al. 2023, Multi-Persona, Exchange-of-Thoughts, ChatEval, AgentVerse) x 9 benchmarks (general knowledge: MMLU, MMLU-Pro, CommonsenseQA, ARC-Challenge, AGIEval; math: GSM8K, MATH; programming: HumanEval, MBPP) x 4 models (GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-haiku, Llama3.1-8b, Llama3.1-70b), vs SA/CoT/SC baselines, debate rounds adjusted so every MAD method uses ~6 LLM calls; 3 repetitions with std (===== PDF PAGE 1, 6, 7 =====). HEADLINE: no MAD method exceeds a 20% win rate vs CoT across 36 scenarios; SoM/EoT/ChatEval/AgentVerse win ~15%, MP 0%; worse on programming, relatively better on math; the gap widens vs self-consistency at comparable LLM-call or token budgets (===== PDF PAGE 3, 7-8 =====). RECONCILIATION: MAD beats direct single-agent prompting in 34/45 GPT-4o-mini conditions—'perfectly aligns with previous findings'—but SoM and ChatEval were never compared to CoT in their original papers, so Du-style positives hold only against the weakest baseline (===== PDF PAGE 8 =====). HYPERPARAMETERS: agents 3->9, rounds 2->4 yield mostly stagnation or decline (sole exception EoT on GSM8K), ruling out misconfiguration as a universal explanation (===== PDF PAGE 8-9 =====). EFFICIENCY: SC converts extra tokens into accuracy; MAD is flat (SoM on MMLU) or trails SC at comparable tokens (EoT); per-question analysis shows aggressive methods (MP/ChatEval/AgentVerse) correct many errors but flip many correct answers, while conservative ones (SoM/EoT) avoid new errors but correct few—a correction/instability trade-off (===== PDF PAGE 9, 25 =====). HETEROGENEITY: Heter-MAD (each generation queries a random model from {GPT-4o-mini, Llama3.1-70b}, p=0.5) improves every tested framework (+6.4% SoM, +8.2% EoT vs single-model averages; up to +5.8% vs CoT-Average), with gains concentrated where models have complementary solvability and in simpler frameworks—'a universal antidote' (===== PDF PAGE 1, 4, 10-13 =====). POSITIONING: credits Du et al. 2023 as foundational but attributes MAD's overvaluation to fragmented, selective evaluation (Table 5 shows minimal benchmark overlap across prior MAD papers); aligns with Smit et al. 2024's null while dismissing its medical-only scope; flags that agents debate whole responses yet rebut final-answer differences rather than reasoning, and that current benchmarks need only single knowledge points (===== PDF PAGE 2, 5, 13, 14, 15 =====). Key identification gap for the root note: no heterogeneous self-consistency control, so the debate-specific value of heterogeneity over plain decorrelated sampling is not identified.
